title: Personal Credit Cards: a card that owes nothing at closure keeps no autopay
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: amount owed at closure and the autopay left on the card

This rule belongs to the Personal Credit Cards line. When a cardholder confirms the closure of a card, the automatic payment option left on the closed card depends first on what the card still owes.

## Rule

1. The option left on the closed card is decided from the card's current amount owed at handling time.
2. A card still owes something only when that amount is above zero.
3. When the amount owed is zero or below, the option left on the closed card is none, because autopay continues only until the amount owed reaches zero.

## Input, judgement, output (hypothetical figures)

| Card's current amount owed at handling time | Something still owed | Option left on the closed card |
|---|---|---|
| 1325.10 USD | yes | decided by the card's autopay arrangements |
| 0.00 USD | no | none |
| minus 4.20 USD, a credit | no | none |

## Points of judgement

- A card that has been paid down to exactly zero before closure leaves no automatic payment running: its option is none.
- A card in credit at closure likewise keeps no automatic payment; there is nothing for autopay to collect.
- The amount examined is the current one at handling time, so a credit posted earlier in the same handling is already reflected in it.
